correctness.rationale: The statement is quantified for every integer \(n\ge5\) and real \(\alpha>0\), with intrinsic circle distances and each reciprocal pair weighted once. A mutual pair corresponds exactly to a local minimum of the cyclic Dirichlet gaps. Gamma normalization converts the count--weighted-length covariance into an exponential local-moment covariance. Diagonal and neighbor terms cancel; each distance-two term equals \(\Gamma(\alpha+1)[3^{-(\alpha+1)}-5^{-(\alpha+1)}]/6\) by a two-region absolutely convergent integral. There are exactly two distance-two indices for \(n\ge5\), establishing the formula and strict positivity. Gamma asymptotics yield \(n^{1-\alpha}\) with positive constant. The standalone checker ran 69 independent exact rational equalities for n=5..8, integer exponents zero through three; finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: An actual semantic-record search and comparison with close full primary works found no statement that implies the all-real-positive-power exact circular covariance. Penrose--Wade treat whole directed length, Bahadir--Ceyhan unweighted reflexive-pair counts, and the two closest published calculations concern circular whole-directed length or interval reciprocal ordinary length. The last contains reusable interior local moments and an identical limiting power-one constant, which is explicitly acknowledged. These ingredients do not themselves give the all-alpha circular closed-form covariance and positive sign/scale classification without new weighted mixed-moment analysis. Historical priority remains qualified; absence in searches alone is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The exact all-alpha formula may be a corollary of an older or broader weighted-nearest-neighbor theorem not discovered in the finite searches.

No independent external scientific validation or proof of absolute historical priority was performed.

value.rationale: The power parameter is a standard substantive design choice in geometric network length/cost statistics, not an arbitrary sampled integer. The theorem gives a full finite-sample count--cost covariance kernel against every real power, strict positive association across the family and an exact threshold in covariance scaling at exponent one, including the nonobvious constant 16/675. It contrasts with previously established negative count dependence on the total directed nearest-neighbor length in precisely the same circle model. These facts cannot be inferred from the separate marginal laws; they give an exact multiscale benchmark for reciprocal-edge geometry. The contribution is a natural complete one-parameter law, not a general theorem for other sampling densities or dimensions.
